newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts lose on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts lose on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Friday in another sluggish session, with front months losing ground on bearish weather forecasts but still finishing above technical support, industry sources said.
April slipped 1.7 cents to close at $1.821 per million British thermal units. May settled 0.4 cent lower at $1.875. Others ended mixed, with 1998s scoring gains.

"I'm not sure how much further it can go. There's no more bearish news out there. What else is going to take it down?" said one Midwest trader, noting mild weather next week may generate some southern cooling demand and support prices.
While the fundamental picture remained mostly bearish, some traders said cratering summer strip prices this week seemed to stir utility interest.
"Some utilities are looking at these numbers as value. I think the downside (in April) is limited to the $1.60s," the Midwest trader said.

Technical traders said the market was still range-bound, with April support at $1.80 and resistance in the $1.93 area. Further buying was likely in the mid-$1.70s and then at the contract low of $1.701. Good selling was expected at $2.04.

In the cash, Gulf Coast gas notionally was talked steady to down slightly in the mid-$1.70s. Midcon pipes also were pegged little changed in the mid-$1.60s. New York city gate baseload quotes ranged from $2.07-2.11, down slightly.
The 12-month strip rose 0.3 cent to $2.022. NYMEX said an estimated 21,486 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 23,441.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Friday.

On the KCBT, April finished two cents higher at $1.63, while deferreds ended up by 1.5 to 2.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.7 cents to 19.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 72 lots changed hands, down from Thursday's total of 86.
